common_topics.label: Current intent and outcome maturity
common_topics.why: Distinguishes briefing, resumption, local change, tool creation, and product execution.
questions: What do you need now: a new concept, continuation, clarification, repair, evaluation, or a change to the agent?
What result is due at this stage, and where should work stop?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Recover existing answers from the actual request and current state.

common_topics.label: Current sources, decisions, and inherited context
common_topics.why: Preserves accepted intent and avoids repeated questions.
questions: Which supplied source is current if they conflict?
What has already been accepted and must survive this continuation?
decisions: Current decisions, amendments, and change impact
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Read available originals, state, hashes, and prior answers first.

common_topics.label: Recipient, real context, and value
common_topics.why: Ties the result to a person, action, and observable improvement.
questions: Who needs the result and in what real situation?
How do they do this now and what should improve?
Who uses, pays for, operates, and accepts the result?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Distinguish roles when they exist.

common_topics.label: Complete target, launch, and trial
common_topics.why: Preserves ambition and distinguishes production sequence from a change in goal.
questions: What does the complete accepted result look like?
What belongs in the first release and what belongs in a separate experiment?
Which simplifications, substitutions, or lost properties are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Keep the full goal visible alongside a bounded test.

common_topics.label: Priorities, examples, and counterexamples
common_topics.why: Turns quality expectations into domain requirements and dependencies.
questions: What matters most in this idea, and why?
Which concrete example is close to the intended result and which features fit?
What would meet the wording but still be unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Preserve exact examples and priorities with their sources.

common_topics.label: Constraints, milestones, and dependencies
questions: Which deadlines, dependent events, and required interim results already exist?
Which hard requirements, compatibility constraints, or external dependencies must remain?
Which choices do you delegate and which do you want to make yourself?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Use actual owner constraints for time, platforms, and features.

common_topics.label: Budget, time, resources, and trade-offs
common_topics.why: Establishes a feasible route and the cost of quality.
questions: Which budget, time, devices, subscriptions, assets, and help are already available?
Which one-time and recurring costs are accepted and which require a decision?
How should we choose if the desired quality exceeds current resources?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify actual prices when binding an operation.

common_topics.label: Materials, rights, and immutable originals
common_topics.why: Identifies legal use, editing, and transfer of actual materials.
questions: Which existing text, design, code, brands, voices, and other materials must be used?
What can be edited, generated, published, or transferred, and who owns the rights?
Which originals or attribution must be retained?
common_topics.applies_when: When using or producing materials. Track missing evidence of rights separately.

common_topics.label: Data, access, privacy, and lifecycle
common_topics.why: Identifies architecture constraints from sensitive or persistent data.
questions: Which data is needed, who controls it, and who may access it?
What must be remembered, synchronized, exported, or deleted?
Which losses, errors, or revoked-access consequences are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: When the result reads, produces, or stores data. Check privacy even for minimal context.

common_topics.label: External actions, risk, and owner steps
common_topics.why: Separates preparation and authorized external effects.
questions: Which external effects are authorized: account changes, messages, publication, payments, or service activation?
Which actions require your involvement or a separate decision?
How should work stop, revert, or check an interrupted result?
common_topics.applies_when: When external actions are possible. Carry valid exact permission forward.

common_topics.label: Environment, capability, and handoff
questions: Where should this result run, where will you operate it, and where should outputs return?
Which hosts, tools, accounts, and target devices have been verified?
How should work transfer, and what must the receiver verify?
common_topics.applies_when: When tooling, installation, execution, or a transfer is needed. Check actual operations.

common_topics.label: Acceptance, evidence, and independence
common_topics.why: Specifies what establishes the stage outcome.
questions: What behavior or artifact will you inspect to accept the result?
Which errors, boundaries and recovery cases must be shown?
Where do you need an independent expert, actual user, device, or post-launch observation?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Check actual use and domain quality separately from schemas or checklists.

common_topics.label: Research, unknowns, and future decisions
common_topics.why: Resolves material gaps without requiring the owner to invent answers.
questions: Which choices need research and a recommendation?
Which researched option best matches your criteria, and do you accept the recommendation?
Which details can be decided later within bounds, and by what milestone?
decisions: Owner, baseline or range, due gate and reopening trigger for deferrals
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Resolve applicable material unknowns before accepting the execution plan.

topics.label: Full game promise
topics.why: Separates the complete game, release scope, and risk probe.
questions: Who should players feel like, what decisions do they make, and what changes as they gain experience?
What is the full target game, what belongs in the first release, and what does the nearest probe test?
decisions: Separate full target, launch and probe scopes
topics.applies_when: For a new game, a change of ambition, or recovery of incomplete context.

topics.label: Route and maturity
topics.why: Selects the needed dependencies from actual state.
questions: What is needed now: search, concept selection, design, built game, audit, repair, release, or operations?
Which accepted decisions, originals, code, builds, and evidence exist, and where are current versions?
decisions: Entry route and actual upstream inputs
Required maturity C0, C1, or T and current scope
topics.applies_when: At intake and whenever the task changes.

topics.label: Platforms and play context
topics.why: Device, grip, and camera inform rules and feasibility before engine selection.
questions: On which devices and in what situation will people play, and which orientation, controls, or camera decisions are fixed?
Which features and quality must be consistent across platforms, and which differences are permitted?
decisions: Platform scope, devices, and sensory requirements
Material limits for camera, input, and parity
topics.applies_when: When platform or input affects the authorized outcome. Reuse answered decisions.

topics.label: System applicability and early dependencies
topics.why: Derives relevant systems from the game.
questions: Which systems are required or excluded, such as narrative, combat, physics, items, economy, networking, or shared play?
Which later requirements change the concept, content sources, saving, or cost now?
topics.applies_when: For full-game planning, system changes, or gap analysis. Missing tools remain blocked.

topics.label: Studio identity and continuity
topics.why: Carries the approved master and rights into later stages.
questions: Does a studio name, mark, or accepted master already exist, and which wording or original bytes must be retained?
What should the studio evoke and which examples or unwanted associations explain that?
topics.applies_when: When creating, resuming, or changing the studio.

topics.label: Brand sources and exports
topics.why: Produces reproducible sources and required placements.
questions: Where will the identity appear: icons, store, game, site, video, or elsewhere?
Which editable sources, fonts, sonic mark, and export formats exist or are needed?
topics.applies_when: When creating a brand or portable studio package.

topics.label: Public and legal identity
topics.why: Names, contacts, and markets affect accounts and agreements.
questions: What publisher name, public contacts, and countries or markets are chosen?
Which legal, tax, or payout confirmations must the owner do, and which actions are authorized for assistance?
decisions: Separate public and legal facts and status
topics.applies_when: For actual account setup, publication, payment, or ownership.

topics.label: Services and accounts
topics.why: Tracks current store, analytics, and support readiness from evidence.
questions: Which stores, analytics, ads, storage, and support channels are already in use?
Who owns accounts, what access exists, and which costs or settings are authorized?
decisions: Authorized setup and exact owner steps
topics.applies_when: When needed for the selected route. Add network or paid services only within actual scope.

topics.label: Studio rights ledger
topics.why: Checks each planned use and source transfer.
questions: Which materials are owned, partner-supplied, or licensed, and what proves the terms?
Do we need commercial use, editing, source redistribution, or reuse in other games?
topics.applies_when: For each external mark, font, audio file, image, or template.

topics.label: Players, needs, and alternatives
topics.why: Audience and real alternatives determine the promise and how to test interest.
questions: Which players and situations are we targeting, and what do they already enjoy or abandon?
Which observations, feedback, or research exist, and what remains a hypothesis?
topics.applies_when: For a new search or change in audience.

topics.label: Search direction and limits
topics.why: The brief defines candidate count and meaningful diversity.
questions: Which genres, fantasies, scales, or references should we explore or exclude, and why?
What finishes the search, and which existing candidates merit continuation?
decisions: Finite search scope and stop rule
Axes of diversity and saved favorites
topics.applies_when: When searching, comparing, or continuing concepts.

topics.label: Fantasy and causal core
topics.why: The premise must yield clear actions and different choices.
questions: Who does the player portray, what do they do in an ordinary situation, and why would they do it again?
What changes if they act now, later, differently, or do nothing?
decisions: Core actions, stakes, and interaction loops
Causal examples and rejection criteria for a narrow demo
topics.applies_when: For every candidate. Develop specific mechanics from accepted intent.

topics.label: Interactions and contextual resources
topics.why: Depth comes from how rules change decisions.
questions: Which traits, tools, materials, or resources change player choices?
Where does using one resource open one opportunity and close another, and how does the player read and recover from that?
decisions: Resource roles, limits, and a counterexample to a universal strategy
topics.applies_when: For every complete concept. Include combat, inventory, or currency only where relevant.

topics.label: World, situations, and novelty
topics.why: Topology and situation grammar shape choices and production capacity.
questions: How does the world connect situations, and which parts change through play?
Where do new challenges come from, and what makes authored or generated situations meaningfully different?
decisions: Novelty, authored components, and launch capacity
topics.applies_when: When the game has spaces, levels, challenges, encounters, or repeatable situations.

topics.label: Actors, risk, and failure
topics.why: The world and other actors should offer legible counters and recovery.
questions: What responds to the player: rivals, allies, physics, time, or another mechanism?
What do risk, mistake, failure, and retry look like, and what does the player keep or lose?
topics.applies_when: For each candidate. AI and enemies are optional. Explain action consequences.

topics.label: Progression, mastery, and returning
topics.why: Later play should change capability and understanding.
questions: How do first play, practiced play, and long-term return differ?
Which capability changes a familiar decision, and why return after the first completion?
decisions: Replay hypothesis and finite launch scope
topics.applies_when: For every complete concept. Derive duration and upgrade counts from scope.

topics.label: Complete input grammar
topics.why: Ergonomics depends on real simultaneous intentions.
questions: Which intentions involve simultaneous, sequential, held, aimed, or cancelled actions?
Which grip, gestures, precision, controllers, and access options fit, and where is peak input load?
decisions: Intent, gestures, actions, simultaneous load and cancellation
Grip, orientation, access, and ergonomic test
topics.applies_when: For each candidate before illustration. Derive control and contact count from play.

topics.label: Camera and readability
topics.why: Framing changes decisions, production, and the meaning of references.
questions: What must the player see before and during actions, and what framing and subject scale support it?
How do camera, HUD and essential cues behave in ordinary, peak and late play?
topics.applies_when: For each visual candidate before image generation.

topics.label: Artistic promise and feasible production
topics.why: Illustration needs a feasible path to actual sources, motion, and scene assembly.
questions: Which specific style, movement, light, materials, and sound define the experience?
Which accepted originals and counterexamples exist, and which production work needs early proof?
decisions: Art direction by element and state
Available production profile and risky representative slice
topics.applies_when: For each candidate with a creative promise, especially before generating or showing imagery.

topics.label: Pricing model and purchase value
topics.why: Commerce follows game value and a complete base path.
questions: Which experience remains complete in the base game, and what extra value might players knowingly pay for?
Which models suit research for this audience, and which are excluded, including ads, subscriptions, or paid randomness?
decisions: Candidate models including no extra offers
Value hypotheses, free path, and allowed paid advantage
topics.applies_when: For a new game or commerce change. Select its own suitable model.

topics.label: Purchased experience in the same gameplay context
topics.why: Checks the actual alternative and cumulative effects.
questions: How do baseline and purchased paths change decisions, pace, options, and trade-offs in the same situation?
How can players understand and try the value, and what happens after multiple purchases or with no purchase?
decisions: Paid, earned, and no-offer comparison and repeat use
Total access and power and competitive limits
topics.applies_when: When proposing purchases, rewarded ads, subscriptions, or expansions.

topics.label: Persistence, networking, and social play
topics.why: Identity and authority affect play and costs before backend selection.
questions: What must survive exit, device change, or long absence?
Does the game need offline play, shared play, competition, accounts, or sharing, and what value does each add?
decisions: Continuation model and conditional online/social scope
Early authority, privacy, and service cost
topics.applies_when: For a complete concept. Add cloud, backend, and social capability only where needed.

topics.label: Complete C1 and concept selection
topics.why: Selection uses complete concepts and their actual risks.
questions: Which strengths and risks determine selection, and what would disqualify a candidate?
What needs a small probe before selection, and which numeric settings can wait with range, method and due date?
decisions: Discriminating tests and actual owner choice
topics.applies_when: Before presenting a concept as complete or moving the selected game into production.

topics.label: Launch inventory and authoring
topics.why: Producers need the complete content scope or exact construction grammar.
questions: Which families, variants, situations, modes, and endings belong to launch?
Which content is authored, generated, or editable after release, and who will operate it?
topics.applies_when: Before the T production handoff.

topics.label: Rules, calculations, and time
topics.why: Typed rules settle behavior before implementation.
questions: Which rules, time windows, priorities, states, and interactions are accepted?
Which parameters need an expert baseline, interval, tuning method, and counterexamples?
decisions: Typed behavior, state, RNG, units, and simulation order
Exact baseline, tolerances, and T fixtures
topics.applies_when: For all active rules. Delegate technical details and bring material design changes to the owner.

topics.label: Physics, contact, and feedback
topics.why: Motion and contact need units, solver mapping, and observable effects.
questions: What should motion, collisions, mass, surfaces, breakage, or manipulation feel like?
Where do simulation and authored motion determine behavior, and which risky contacts need an early scene?
decisions: Fixed tick, contact adapter, crash behavior, and representative fixtures
topics.applies_when: When physics or kinematic movement affects decisions or feel.

topics.label: Damage, failure, and recovery
topics.why: Separates contact, damage, and lifecycle rules.
questions: Which events cause damage, malfunction, death, loss or completion, and how does the player anticipate them?
Which defenses, repeated contacts, simultaneous events, recovery, and exceptions change outcomes?
topics.applies_when: When damage, crash, defeat, or other failure applies. Use HP only where suitable.

topics.label: Abilities, equipment, and compatibility
topics.why: Defines distinct strategies and valid compositions.
questions: Which ability families and properties create different approaches?
Which slots, conflicts, synergies, limits, and realistic opportunities govern compatibility?
topics.applies_when: When abilities, tools, vehicles, items, builds, or equivalent mechanics apply.

topics.label: World and situation generation
topics.why: Preserves solvability, pacing, and meaningful novelty.
questions: Which places, transitions, routes, and persistent consequences belong to the world?
What sets legality and novelty, and what happens after generation fails?
decisions: Topology and authored or generated content
Constraints, RNG version, repair and fallback, novelty signature
topics.applies_when: For worlds, levels, procedural challenges, encounters, or other content grammar.

topics.label: Actors, perception, and AI
topics.why: Limits AI knowledge and establishes visible counterplay.
questions: What can each actor sense, remember, and do in response?
How do roles, phases, movement, coordination, and errors differ, and which player actions change AI choices?
decisions: Encounter and boss state, counterplay fixtures
topics.applies_when: When system-controlled actors exist. Add opponents only if required.

topics.label: Lore, knowledge, and story consequences
topics.why: Tracks canon, conditions, and history of decisions.
questions: Which canon, characters, factions, knowledge, and themes affect play?
How do actions change quests, dialogue, world reactions, and character knowledge, and what persists?
topics.applies_when: When story, dialogue, quests, or reactive lore applies.

topics.label: Progression and rewards
topics.why: Connects unlocks to actual use, pace, and consequence.
questions: Which prerequisites, temporary or permanent changes, and specialization limits apply?
When are rewards granted, where can they be used, and what happens with duplicates, limits, or a failed grant?
decisions: Curves, grant behavior, early/mid/late and return examples
topics.applies_when: When progression, rewards, collections, or replay applies.

topics.label: Economy and complete offers
topics.why: Aligns prices, resources, entitlements, and actual value.
questions: Which sources and sinks, exchange, limits, expiration, and offer frequency fit this model?
How do time to goal, access, and strength differ for earned and paid portfolios, and how is the purchase understood?
decisions: Offer value, trial, eligibility, ownership, expiry, no-offer fixtures
topics.applies_when: When resources, sales, rewarded ads, or paid rights apply.

topics.label: Input recognition and camera policy
topics.why: Separates intent, recognition, action, and presentation.
questions: How do different states, concurrent gestures, focus loss, cancellation, and UI capture recognize each intent?
Who owns each touch and camera request, and how do tracking, aim, manual input, and scripted shots arbitrate?
decisions: Camera arbitration, cancellation, accessibility, peak-load cases
topics.applies_when: For the selected game before implementation of controls and production UI.

topics.label: Complete journey, learning, and accessibility
topics.why: Covers first use, errors, interruptions, and resumption.
questions: How do players move through first launch, learning, ordinary sessions, failure, exit, and return?
Which settings, locales, legibility, assists, reduced motion, and alternatives to sound or haptics matter?
decisions: Screens, states, transitions, and learning context
Predictive, confirmation, error, recovery, and access cues
topics.applies_when: For every selected game. Include interface and system states actually in scope.

topics.label: Visual, motion, music, and haptic production
topics.why: Translates the reference into sources, events, and assembly.
questions: Which forms, materials, lights, rigs or clips, effects, music, sounds, and haptics support each major state?
How do action, contact, and multimodal feedback stay consistent and informative with channels off?
decisions: Creative production contracts and finite inventory
Source, export, import, and scene recipes with parity tolerances
topics.applies_when: For all required creative media in the selected game.

topics.label: State, authority, and continuation
topics.why: Sets durable boundaries for purchases, progression, and world.
questions: Which states are durable, reconstructible, transient, cached, or secret, and when can a reward or spend be confirmed?
What happens offline, after crashes, clock changes, device conflicts, schema upgrades, or account deletion?
decisions: State catalogue, simulation and durable boundaries, consistency groups
topics.applies_when: For mutable state. Cloud and accounts apply only if selected.

topics.label: Engine, native path, and budgets
topics.why: Matches architecture to the accepted platforms and craft.
questions: Which actual engines, SDKs, hosts, devices, and production tools meet the target?
Which frame rate and pacing, memory, heat, power, loading, and download budgets should the representative slice verify?
decisions: Researched alternatives and engine or renderer decision
Pinned toolchain, devices, and measured budgets
topics.applies_when: Before technical choice and costly production. Bring material quality trade-offs to the owner.

topics.label: Data, security, and conditional networking
topics.why: External and network components change authority, privacy, and operations.
questions: What specific value do each SDK, account, server, social or multiplayer feature add?
What data, rights, abuse risk, age limits, and external costs result?
decisions: Conditional network and platform contracts and operating owners
topics.applies_when: When networking, external SDKs, accounts, ads, or data collection applies.

topics.label: T handoff and evidence plan
topics.why: Settles material product choices before dependent production.
questions: Which scenarios, boundaries, and counterexamples verify important promises?
What must be exact before implementation, which probe runs first, and which device or human proof comes later?
decisions: T package usable without chat history
Oracles, dependencies, owners, due proof, and tuning limits
topics.applies_when: Before implementing accepted scope or its materially affected dependencies.

topics.label: Asset coverage and lineage
topics.why: Covers approved categories, states, and variants.
questions: Which exact master revisions and accepted originals govern each item?
Which characters, items, spaces, UI, states, views, locales, and variants does the accepted inventory require?
decisions: Source, export, and import IDs and hashes
Full denominator and remaining item blockers
topics.applies_when: For each production asset package.

topics.label: Editable sources and production path
topics.why: Required mesh, rig, vectors, and music projects need their own source.
questions: What actual source format does the consumer need, and which tools deliver the accepted quality?
Which missing views, construction, rigging, or materials need a material creative decision?
topics.applies_when: When making or repairing creative sources.

topics.label: Motion, rig, and contact
topics.why: Movement must conform to mechanics, collision, and identity.
questions: Which clips, states and transitions, blends, IK and constraints, and events support action and recovery?
How will we check support, grip, weight, collision, and moving silhouette from the gameplay camera?
topics.applies_when: For animated actors, vehicles, items, environment, or UI.

topics.label: Music, sound, and in-context listening
topics.why: Reviews the complete intended audio experience in applicable states.
questions: Which phrases, loops, transitions, stems, ambience, voices, and effects does the event matrix require?
Who will listen, where, and how will they check seams, dynamics, priority, synchronization, and ducking?
decisions: Contextual audition, mix and quality findings
topics.applies_when: When audio is in scope. Missing tools are a blocker.

topics.label: Accessible VFX, interface, and haptics
topics.why: Keeps information available across settings.
questions: Which cues, HUD, typography, safe areas, and locale states are required in ordinary and peak scenes?
How does an essential event remain readable without color, sound, vibration, or with reduced motion?
topics.applies_when: For every creative channel conveying information.

topics.label: Scene assembly and representative slice
topics.why: Requires a real path from source through export to native runtime before scaling.
questions: Which scene represents the most consequential motion, contact, camera, HUD, audio, and peak load?
Which exact imports, settings, budgets, and comparisons to the original establish acceptance?
decisions: Actual import, context and parity evidence or exact blocker
topics.applies_when: Before scale-up and after changes to shared rig, shaders, audio, or import.

topics.label: Rights, tools, and transfer
topics.why: Checks lawful use in runtime and delivery to the consumer.
questions: What rights, attribution, commercial terms, and redistribution limits apply to sources and tools?
Which third-party or paid production operations are needed, and does authority cover them?
decisions: Allowed route and actual package bytes and manifest
topics.applies_when: For external materials, paid tools, or a package transfer.

topics.label: Actual toolchain and platform artifacts
topics.why: Distinguishes source, build, signing, and installation.
questions: Which exact toolchain versions, native hosts, signature routes, and devices are actually available?
Which artifacts are due per platform, and which steps require owner-only access?
decisions: Pinned build recipes and output per platform
Actual capabilities and launch or return transfer
topics.applies_when: At implementation start or when changing the toolchain or native route.

topics.label: Integrate rules, data, and assets
topics.why: Binds implementation to current accepted data and sources.
questions: Which contracts, data, assets, and accepted references govern each behavior?
Where are incompatible interfaces, undefined rules, or material changes from accepted intent?
decisions: Dependency repair or approved material change
topics.applies_when: For implemented scope. Return unresolved product decisions to Design.

topics.label: Runtime input, camera, and lifecycle
topics.why: Observes causal effects of actions, cancellations, and interruptions.
questions: How do concurrent intentions, cancel, focus loss, UI capture, and camera arbitration behave?
Which captures and input traces show ordinary, peak, and failure paths on the claimed device?
topics.applies_when: For interactive gameplay implementation.

topics.label: Sensory fidelity in runtime
topics.why: Compares the actual motion, sound, and scene to the accepted reference.
questions: Which runtime captures, actual listening, and physical haptic tests are due?
Where do art, motion, contact, sound or interface differ from the original, and do they meet tolerance?
topics.applies_when: For creative channels in the selected scope.

topics.label: Content, generation, and authoring tools
topics.why: Covers the accepted inventory and repeatable editing.
questions: Does the build cover the finite launch catalogue or the selected grammar with limits and fallback?
How does an author add and validate content, translations, or configuration without hidden developer steps?
decisions: Complete content and versioned authoring process
topics.applies_when: For content systems or a launch catalogue.

topics.label: Saves, recovery, and migration
topics.why: Protects progress against lost and duplicate state.
questions: How do durable grants and spending, crash recovery, conflicts, migration, and rollback limits work?
Which kill, interruption, offline, clock, and device-change fixtures verify invariants?
decisions: State authority and actual persistence adapters
Failure, recovery, migration fixtures and evidence
topics.applies_when: For mutable durable state.

topics.label: Purchases, rewards, and entitlements
topics.why: Requires idempotent reconciliation across financial failures.
questions: How do actual sandbox purchase, restore, refund, revoke, pending, and offline affect entitlements and state?
How does the game prevent duplicate grants or lost rights after timeout, retry, reinstall, or device change?
decisions: Actual sandbox receipts and combined paid and earned regression
topics.applies_when: When purchases, rewarded ads, or external entitlements apply.

topics.label: Sustained load on target devices
topics.why: Measures stability across representative play.
questions: Which representative devices and peak tasks measure FPS, frame pacing, memory, heat, power, and load time?
Which optimization preserves accepted quality, and which material deviation requires a decision?
topics.applies_when: For claimed native platforms and performance targets.

topics.label: Runtime privacy, network, and failures
topics.why: Verifies actual external access and recovery behavior.
questions: How do authentication, permissions, consent, deletion, SDK inventory, and secret-safe configuration work?
What do players see during network failure, server incompatibility, abuse, or loss of account?
decisions: Security, privacy, and network failure cases
topics.applies_when: When accounts, SDKs, backend, multiplayer, social interaction, or telemetry apply.

topics.label: Frozen candidate and coverage denominator
topics.why: Binds a verdict to exact bytes and criteria.
questions: Which exact source, build, configuration, data, and asset revisions are frozen?
Which musts, platforms, devices, and criteria are independently checked and which evidence remains valid?
decisions: Independent review scope and current evidence
topics.applies_when: Before every QA verdict and after a material change.

topics.label: Causality, depth, and variation
topics.why: Verifies the entire game promise from actual decisions.
questions: Do mechanics, resources, and context change decisions, or does one strategy dominate?
Do new capabilities reframe earlier tasks and do early, mid, late, return, and generated situations differ?
decisions: Gameplay, progression, world, and content defects
topics.applies_when: For active systems and the accepted progression arc.

topics.label: Ergonomics, readability, and feel
topics.why: Uses appropriate media and real participants where required.
questions: Which actual device, motion, listening, and tactile observations confirm controls and creative target?
Do learning, anticipation, peak load, cancellation, access, and critical cues work with channels off?
topics.applies_when: For each claimed interactive or sensory property.

topics.label: Economy, fairness, and financial integrity
topics.why: Separates model evaluation and real sandbox checks.
questions: How do free, earned, low-spend, and paid portfolios differ in access, time to goal, and total advantage?
Do actual receipts cover grant, restore, refund, revoke, retry, offline, and applicable random rewards?
decisions: Economic dominance and entitlement integrity verdict
Remaining purchase, ad, and offer defects
topics.applies_when: When economy, purchases, ads, or paid randomness apply.

topics.label: Interruptions, failures, and compatibility
topics.why: Exercises state loss and version conflicts.
questions: Does the game follow contract through crashes, termination, pause and resume, save conflict, clock change, migration, and deletion?
Which executed fixtures cover network and authentication, corruption, version mismatch and recovery?
topics.applies_when: For active persistence, platform, and network dependencies.

topics.label: Platform and sustained performance
topics.why: Requires actual proof for each claimed platform.
questions: Which exact builds were built, installed, and tested for each platform?
Do representative sustained and peak tests, input and sound interruptions, and device layouts pass?
topics.applies_when: When claiming devices or native readiness.

topics.label: Actual players and evidence limits
topics.why: Bounds findings on interest, understanding, and commerce.
questions: Which actual participants and segments are available, and what will their playtest examine?
Which conclusions follow, and which remain hypotheses due to sample size or bias?
decisions: Limits on enjoyment, learning, retention, and commerce claims
topics.applies_when: When human experience is claimed. Track desk review separately.

topics.label: Defects, regression, and acceptance
topics.why: Requires each blocking must to pass.
questions: Which defects block this gate, who repairs each cause, and which checks need to be rerun?
Which limitations are allowed in scope and what exact creative outcome is the owner accepting?
decisions: Severity, owner, closure, and affected regression
Independent verdict and actual user acceptance
topics.applies_when: At QA closure and after repair.

topics.label: Exact release candidate
topics.why: Pins binaries, configuration, and schemas.
questions: Which signed binaries, content and config epochs, save schemas, symbols, and hashes are included?
Which current QA verdicts, critical gaps, and owner-only signing or account steps remain?
decisions: Exact RC manifest and readiness state
topics.applies_when: Before submission or rollout.

topics.label: Current store requirements
topics.why: Uses policies and SDK rules current at the time of action.
questions: Which storefronts, markets, age groups and content types does release cover?
Which current official SDK, payment, privacy, testing, ads, and disclosure rules apply to the exact candidate?
topics.applies_when: For actual store release. Investigate using the concrete product parameters.

topics.label: Metadata, media, and claims
topics.why: Ensures the listing matches runtime and rights.
questions: Which names, copy, screenshots, video, locales, prices and launch markets are selected?
Does each claim match the build, and which rights, credit, support, and privacy contacts must be shown?
topics.applies_when: When preparing public listings or promotion.

topics.label: Store products and payouts
topics.why: Validates real products, accounts and rights separately from sandbox results.
questions: Which product IDs, prices, availability, entitlements, and state transitions must be active?
Which agreements, tax or payout, or personal confirmations are complete, and which exact receipts show them?
decisions: Unverified finance and account state and exact owner step
topics.applies_when: When release includes sales, ads, subscriptions, or paid rights.

topics.label: Rollout, observation, and recovery
topics.why: Bounds impact and preserves coherent state through failure.
questions: Who receives the release at each stage, and which actual signals stop or expand it?
How can we restore binaries, configuration and content and keep saves and entitlements compatible?
decisions: Measured stop criteria and migration limits
topics.applies_when: Before authorized production rollout.

topics.label: Support and operational ownership
topics.why: Provides a real support and incident path after release.
questions: Where can players report lost progress, purchases, bugs or privacy issues, and who responds?
Which actual crash, analytics, and support signals, alert owners and runbooks are available?
decisions: Support and incident owners and runbooks
Actual observation capability and authorized cadence
topics.applies_when: For beta or public release.

topics.label: Publication and verified result
topics.why: External action needs exact current authority and an actual receipt.
questions: Which exact submission or release action, store, account, version, and rollout are covered?
How do we verify submitted, approved, and released status, and reconcile an unknown provider result?
decisions: Actual job, receipt, status, and read-only reconciliation
topics.applies_when: Immediately before the external effect. Carry forward valid exact approval.

topics.label: Actual production state
topics.why: Uses observed production versions and evidence.
questions: Which versions, content and config epochs, schemas, rollout states, and job results are current?
Which current telemetry, support reports, provider receipts and incidents exist, and what gaps do they have?
topics.applies_when: At operations intake, on resume, or after an unknown provider outcome.

topics.label: Incidents, money, and progress
topics.why: Protects player state while repairing the cause.
questions: What is the actual effect on players, progress, payments, privacy or availability, and how can it be reproduced?
Which smallest authorized mitigation restores coherent state, and which dependencies need QA and release?
decisions: Root cause, migrations or compensation, and regression
topics.applies_when: For outages, payment, save, or privacy defects, or degradation.

topics.label: Players, cohorts, and findings
topics.why: Treats actual behavior within the limits of the data.
questions: What do segments, cohorts, platforms, and earned and paid portfolios show about learning, abandonment and return?
Which claim is supported, what alternative explanations remain, and what should we test next?
topics.applies_when: When evaluating player experience, retention, economy, or commerce.

topics.label: Content growth and novelty
topics.why: Expands useful decisions within production capacity.
questions: Which new capability, situation or story change should introduce a different experience?
How will it change old tasks, world state, content compatibility, and finite production capacity?
decisions: Affected catalogues, states, assets, and continuity
topics.applies_when: When requesting new content, a season, or expansion.

topics.label: Economy, offers, and experiments
topics.why: Accounts for cumulative effects of pricing and rewards.
questions: Which exact problem should a change in price, reward curves, cadence, ads or offers solve?
What changes for existing rights, earned and paid portfolios, time targets, and dominance, and which guardrails and stopping rules apply?
decisions: Versioned experiment or configuration and authorized rollout
topics.applies_when: When changing the economy, monetization, or a live test.

topics.label: Compatibility, rights, and operating cost
topics.why: Tracks platform and dependency changes that affect support.
questions: Which changes in platforms, SDKs, services, rights, cost or devices affect support?
How do we update dependencies, schemas, and runbooks while preserving the experience and recovery?
decisions: Upgrade, deprecation, rights, and affected tests
topics.applies_when: When a relevant change arrives or a maintenance review is authorized.

topics.label: Actual monitoring scope
topics.why: Recurring work requires an authorized running scheduler or service.
questions: Which sources and signals need recurring checks, how often, and who acts on results?
Do you need one investigation, a runbook, or an actually configured authorized schedule?
decisions: Concrete observation scope and action owner
Actual schedule or service and checkpoint
topics.applies_when: When requesting monitoring, reminders, or ongoing support.
